title: Temporal Modality Refinement for Temporal Moment Localization via Language and Video-Image Question Answering Tasks
abstract: In this paper, we focus on a novel task, to introduce a unified platform that deals with multiple research directions. An instance, the goal of temporal moment localization in videos using natural language is to locate the moment that corresponds to the input query, and output is moment/answer of the query. Similar to this, the goal of video and image question answering is to use input questions to locate the correct answer within the video and image. For every task listed above, the input consists of video, image, and query/question, while the output is visual from video or image. We present the first study on a unified framework for chronological modality refinement (CMR) that, offers a single platform to address temporal moment localization, video, and image question answering, elimination of modality entanglement, and successful implementation of modality collaboration. Our CMR include a temporal pyramid (TP) module with $ m $ blocks and a distinctive transformer architecture that takes both video and image as input. To further reinforce the unified design, we introduce a lightweight Unified Task Routing Module (UTRM) that automatically identifies active modality configurations and routes video, image, and language features to their appropriate processing paths, enabling seamless task-adaptive behavior within the unified architecture. This routing mechanism enhances feature consistency across tasks and ensures that temporal, spatial, and linguistic reasoning remain disentangled yet collaborative. Combined with our refinement modules, UTRM significantly improves the generalization ability of CMR across heterogeneous multimodal tasks. We employ various datasets Charades-STA, TACoS, Activity-Net, TGIF-QA, MSVD, and MSRVTT-QA related to above mentioned research directions, and results demonstrate the effectiveness of our CMR approach.
